welcome_lead: Master SN1 vs SN2 substitution at carbon.
meta_desc: A-Level chemistry adventure on SN1 and SN2 mechanisms.
final_note: You sketched every curly arrow with intent.

concepts.def: Departs with bonding e- pair; e.g. Br-.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Nucleophile attacks C from opposite side to leaving group. Transition state has partial bonds to both.

Rate = k[R-X][Nu-]. Inversion of configuration (Walden inversion). Best with 1° R-X due to low steric hindrance.

Step 1 (slow): R-X -> R+ + X-. Step 2 (fast): R+ + Nu- -> R-Nu.

Rate = k[R-X] only. Tertiary R-X favoured (stable carbocation). Racemic mixture from planar cation.

Tertiary, polar protic solvent, weak Nu -> SN1. Primary, polar aprotic, strong Nu -> SN2.

Secondary is in-between. Bulky Nu favours SN1 (or E1); strong Nu/base + heat favours elimination.

free_texts.q: Term for nucleophilic substitution with inversion.
